help.title: General settings
help.text:
The general page is the page where settings like System
frequency , Multi
phase system and Transfer
switch settings are done.

help.title: System frequency
help.text:
Use this setting to specify the frequency of the Multi. This is the
frequency the Multi will make when it is inverting (except when Change
inverter period time when VS is on is checked and the VS is on).
This setting determines also the acceptable frequency range (either
45-55Hz or 55-65Hz) for the transfer switch if Accept
wide input frequency range is disabled.

help.title: AC input current limit
help.text:
Use this setting the specify the maximum input AC current. This value
is important for both the PowerControl and the PowerAssist
function.
Note that, when Overruled
by remote is checked and a remote panel is connected or the
virtual remote panel is used,
the position of the knob on the panel determines the actual AC limit.
The knob will overrule any setting done here!
If your device is equipped with a dual AC input this setting specifies
the maximum input for AC1.
Note that with PowerAssist
enabled there is a minimum value for the AC input current limit. Please
see the note at PowerAssist .

help.title: Use remote current limit for AC1 input
help.text:
Overruled by remote
If this check box is checked the (virtual) remote panel determines the
maximum input AC current for the AC input instead of the AC
input current limit setting.

help.title: AC2 input current limit
help.text:
Use this setting the specify the maximum current on the secondary (=AC2)
mains input. This value is important for both the PowerControl and the PowerAssist
function.
Note that you can specify whether or not the (virtual) remote panel
setting overrules this setting. Use the Overruled
by remote setting for this purpose.
This setting is only available in devices with dual AC input.
When power is applied to both the AC1 and AC2 input the AC1 input has
priority.
Note that with PowerAssist
enabled there is a minimum value for the AC input current limit. Please
see the note at PowerAssist .

help.title: Use remote current limit for AC2 input
help.text:
Overruled by remote (2)
If this check box is checked the (virtual) remote panel determines the
maximum input AC current for the AC2 input instead of the AC2
input current limit setting.
Note that this setting is only available in devices with dual AC input.

help.title: Dynamic current limiter
help.text:
This setting is an expansion of the AC input current limit mechanism.
If disabled, the AC input current limit is specified by the AC
input current limit setting. When this setting is enabled the effective
AC input current limit depends on the load history. When the load is lower
than the AC input current limit
the effective AC input current limit is also lower but slightly above
the load. If the load increases the effective limit also increases with
a delay. The thought behind this is that when a generator is running at
a low load it cannot switch to full load immediately and it needs some
time to increase the power.
An example:
We have a 2kVA generator. We adjust the AC
input current limit setting to 8A and we enable PowerAssist .
We have no load connected and the batteries are fully charged so therefore
no current from generator is drawn. At this moment we connect a load of
7A to the Multi.
Normally the Multi would not react because the load is below the AC input current limit
setting. The result is that the full load is connected to the generator
which will drop in voltage because it cannot deliver that current instantly.
If the output of the generator drops to below the AC
low disconnect limit, the Multi will switch to inverter function and
the back feed relay will open, disconnecting the generator from the load.
If however we had this "Dynamic current limiter" setting enabled
the effective AC input current limit would be far lower than 8A because
the load was zero. So connecting a load of 7A will result in the Multi
starting to Assist and no voltage drop is seen on the output. The generator
will start to supply the load and the effective AC input current limit
will slowly increase to 8A. At that moment the Multi will stop assisting
and the full load is on the generator.
This is a powerful option in combination with PowerAssist
but even with PowerControl it can prevent unnecessary switching
to inverter because the charge current will reduce when AC input current
becomes higher than the effective AC input current limit.

help.title: State of charge when Bulk finsihed
help.text:
State of charge when Bulk finished
Use this setting to specify the amount of charge to which the "state
of charge" is set when during charge the Bulk phase (see picture
below) is finished.
This is needed to prevent a run-away of the "state of charge"
value due to inevitable measurement errors over several charge/discharge
cycles.

help.title: Battery capacity
help.text:
In order for the battery monitor to be able to correctly calculate the
"state of charge" the battery capacity of the connected batteries
must be known.
Use this setting to specify the connected battery capacity in Ah.

help.title: Number of slaves
help.text:
Note: This setting is unavailable
in Multis which use VE.Bus for parallel operation.
A parallel system is build with 1 master and up to 5 slaves. With this
setting one can specify the number of slaves in the system. This setting
has only to be done in the master. Note that it is not required to specify
the number of slaves. The system will work just fine without this setting
being specified.
This setting is added for convenience of the end-user. The only
effect of this setting is on the scaling of the AC
input current limit . If this setting is 0 one must divide the available
AC current by the number of Multis (Slaves + Master) and set the limit
accordingly. So setting the limit to 10A in a parallel system with 3 Multis
would result in a limit of 3*10=30A.
If however in this system the number of slaves is set to 2, then the
division is done internally and setting the limit to 10A will result in
10A for the whole system.
In VE.Bus
systems this scaling is done automatically. Therefore this setting is
not available nor needed in such a system.

help.title: Determining the multi phase type
help.text:
Note: This setting is unavailable
in Multis which use VE.Bus for multi phase operation.
Use this setting to determine the kind of multi-phase required:
3 phase.
Three Multis required. Output is 3-phases with 120° phase shift.
Split phase 180°
Two Multis required. Output is 2 phases with 180° phase shift.
Two leg 3 phase 120°
Two Multis required. Output is 2 phases of a normal 3 phase system
so two phases with 120° phase shift.

help.title: Enable 2-3 phase
help.text:
Note: This setting is unavailable
in Multis which use VE.Bus for multi phase operation.
All the Multis in a multi phase system must have 2-3 phase enabled.
Use this setting to perform this.
If more Multis per phase are connected in parallel then only the masters
of the parallel system must have 2-3 phase enabled.

help.title: Leader
help.text:
Note: This setting is unavailable
in Multis which use VE.Bus for multi phase operation.
In a multi phase system there is always one (and only one) leader. The
Multis for the other phases are called followers. Use this setting to
designate one of the Multis as leader. If this check box is not checked
the Multi is a follower.

help.title: Accept wide input frequency range (45-65 Hz)
help.text:
When enabled all AC input frequency between 45-65 Hz is accepted as
valid. When this setting is disabled the acceptable input frequency is
the System frequency +/- 5Hz.

help.title: AC low disconnect
help.text:
With this setting one can determine the AC input voltage below which
the transfer switch will switch off. This voltage level will always lie
below the AC low connect level.
In fact, changing this level will also change the AC
low connect level.
Note that this setting can be ignored for a short time when UPS
function is disabled.

help.title: AC low connect
help.text:
This setting forms a pair with AC
low disconnect . With this setting one determines the AC low voltage
at which the transfer switch will switch on. This should lie above the
AC low disconnect level to prevent
continuous switching of the transfer switch when the voltage is fluctuating
around that level. Note that in fact the parameter which is changed is
an offset voltage relative to AC
low disconnect . The result of this is that when changing the AC
low disconnect level this "AC low connect" level changes
also!
Newer Multis ( software
versions 18XXXXX, 19XXXXX etc.) will also use this setting during
charge. When the AC input voltage drops due to the increasing charge current
the charger will take care that the voltage does not drop below this level.

help.title: AC high connect
help.text:
This setting forms a pair with AC
high disconnect . With this setting one determines the AC high voltage
at which the transfer switch will switch on. This should lie below the
AC high disconnect level to
prevent continuous switching of the transfer switch when the voltage is
fluctuating around that level. Note that in fact the parameter which is
changed is an offset voltage relative to AC
high disconnect . The result of this is that when changing the AC
high disconnect level this "AC high connect" level changes
also!

help.title: AC high disconnect
help.text:
With this setting one can determine the AC input voltage above which
the transfer switch will switch off. This voltage level will always lie
above the AC high connect level.
In fact changing this level will also change the AC
high connect level.
Multis with software
version 17xx112 and up, 18xxxxx, 19xxxxx or 20xxxxx (where X can be
any number) will also use this setting as a stop condition during PowerAssist .
When this voltage is reached, the Multi will stop with PowerAssist .
In some cases it can be advantageous to lower this value. Inverter based
generators might enter into an error state when the voltage becomes too
high.

help.title: UPS function
help.text:
This setting can be used to enable/disable the fast input voltage detection.
When UPS function is enabled the wave shape of the AC input is tested.
If it is not sinusoidal within certain limits the AC input voltage is
rejected. However certain generators or very weak mains supply have an
ill shaped sinusoidal output, especially when the load suddenly changes.
In such cases a failure will be detected when UPS function is enabled.
One can disable the UPS function in that case. The drawback is a slightly
longer transfer time.
Multis with a software
version starting with 18 or higher will use this setting also in another
way. By disabling UPS function the AC
low disconnect is ignored for a short time when the load current is
higher than 1.5 times the AC
input current limit . This to prevent unnecessary switching to inverter
due to a voltage drop when a high load is connected.

help.title: Inverter settings
help.text:
The inverter page contains all the settings which are related to the
inverter. One can think of Inverter
output voltage , PowerAssist
etc.

help.title: Inverter output voltage
help.text: With this setting one can change the AC output voltage of the inverter.

help.title: Assist current boost factor
help.text:
This setting is a special setting for PowerAssist .
When the Multi is charging and, due to a sudden load, the mains current
exceeds the AC
input current limit the Multi will switch to assist mode (when enabled,
see PowerAssist ).
At that moment the current needed is unknown. The Multi makes an assumption
of the magnitude of this current. This assumption is equal to the AC
input current limit multiplied by this "Assist current boost
factor" setting. The default factor is two. This will prevent the
circuit breaker from tripping because current provided by the inverter
minus the current drawn by the load is always lower than the rating of
the circuit breaker. This, of course, when the AC
input current limit is correctly adjusted to the circuit breaker.
If, for instance in a generator
application , the circuit breaker has a higher value than the AC
input current limit . (Nominal capacity of the generator is lower than
the maximum peak load) and one knows that the load which is switched on
always draws a certain current one can consider to increase this factor
to achieve better results with sudden load changes.

help.title: PowerAssist
help.text:
With this check box the PowerAssist feature can be enabled or disabled.
Use PowerAssist to prevent an external circuit breaker to trip due to
excessive load. If the load exceeds the AC
input current limit the Multi will start inverting in parallel with
the external AC supply and will provide the extra current needed.
Note : When PowerAssist is enabled
there is a minimum AC input current limit depending on the device type. Setting a lower limit than this
minimum will result in the minimum limit. Note that in a parallel system
this limit is per device !

help.title: Ground relay
help.text:
Used to enable/disable the internal ground relay functionality. The
ground relay is useful when an earth-leakage circuit-breaker is part of
the installation.
When the internal transfer switch is open (inverter mode) the Neutral
of the inverter is connected to PE. When the transfer switch closes (AC
input is transferred to the output) the Neutral is first disconnected
from PE.
Warning : Disabling the ground
relay on "120/240V" models (split phase models) will disconnect
the L2 output from the inverter.

help.title: DC input low shut-down
help.text:
With this setting one can determine the low battery voltage level at
which the inverter will switch off. This can be useful to prevent drawing
to much current from an exhausted battery. This voltage level will always
lie below the DC input low restart
level. In fact changing this level will also change the DC
input low restart level.

help.title: DC input low restart
help.text:
This setting forms a pair with DC
input low shut-down . With this setting one determines the battery
voltage at which the inverter will switch on. Note that in fact the parameter
which is changed is an offset voltage relative to DC
input low shut-down . The result of this is that, when changing the
DC input low shut-down level,
this "DC input low restart" level changes also!

children.name: UBatPreAlarmOffsetEdit
children.hint: Note: This setting is linked to DC input low restart
children.label: DC input low pre-alarm

help.title: DC input low alarm
help.text:
DC input low pre-alarm
With this setting one can determine the level at which the Low batter
pre-alarm indication starts.
Note that in fact the parameter which is changed is an offset voltage
relative to the DC input low restart
level which in its turn is relative to the DC
input low shut-down level. The result of this is that,
when changing either one of DC
input low restart and DC
input low shut-down , this "DC input low pre-alarm" level
changes also!
Note: The alarm level (not the pre-alarm!) is always linked to the DC input low shut-down
level.

help.title: Start limit for low power (AES) mode
help.text:
If the load is lower than this setting (for some time) the Inverter
will switch to AES mode.
(See also Hysteresis
on limit for low power (AES) mode .)
Note 1
The real setting inside the device is a current setting (in Amps) and
not a power setting (in Watts).
The program converts this to a power figure for convenience. With low
load this results in a significant deviation because there is a
small (constant) imaginary current which cannot be neglected anymore.
The effect is that the actual limit in Watts is lower than the setting
indicates.
Note 2
Changes in the AES limit settings will become effective after the device
is reset. (So switch the device off and on with front switch.)

help.title: Hysteresis on limit for low power (AES) mode
help.text:
If the inverter is in AES mode and the load is higher than this setting
added to the Start
limit for low power (AES) mode the Inverter will switch to normal
mode.
Please read notes 1 and 2 at Start
limit for low power (AES) mode !

help.title: AES type
help.text:
The inverter supports two methods of power reduction (not available
on all models) when there is no or low load connected.
Both of them change the output of the inverter.
Method 1
The first method is called "modified sine wave". The inverter
changes the wave shape as shown below:
This waveshape reduces the RMS value of the output while it maintains
the peak voltage. This will result in a lower power consumption.
Method 2
The second method is called "search mode" and it will reduce
the power consumption even further than the "modified sine wave"
method. The output is switched off during most of the time and approximate
once per 2 seconds the output is switched on as shown below. When a load
is detected the output will remain on.
Disadvantage of this option is that it can take some time (at most about
1 second) before the inverter detects that a load is connected.
If this is unacceptable one should choose the "modified sine wave"
option.

help.title: Enable AES
help.text:
With this check box the AES feature can be enabled or disabled. Use
this setting to save battery energy when there is no (or very low) load
connected to the inverter. When the load on the inverter is low the inverter
switches to a special AES mode in which less current is drawn from battery.
When the load increases the inverter will switch to normal mode again.
Switching from no load to full load can take slightly more time when
AES is enabled. Therefore it may be advantageous to disable the AES in
some applications.
The load limits for entering and leaving the AES mode and the AES type
can be set with the following settings (not available on all devices): Start limit for
low power (AES) mode , Hysteresis
on limit for low power (AES) mode and AES
type .
Important note:
AES settings will be ignored when the device is part of a VE.Bus system. In other words: "AES
will function only when the device is working stand-alone."

help.text:
The charger page contains all the settings which are related to the
charger. For convenience a charge curve is also on this page. This curve

help.text:
With this check box the internal charger can be enabled or disabled.
This can be useful when an external charger is used and one does not need
the internal charger but one wants to use the internal
transfer switch .

help.title: Default battery
help.text:
This button can be used to setup the charger part for a specific type
of battery.
Note that default battery is
actually not a setting and is not stored in the device . This mechanism is just provided for
convenience. Selecting a default battery will adapt the Absorption
voltage , Float voltage ,
(Maximum) Absorption
time and Charge curve
settings.
Changing any of these settings will change the battery type. If the
new settings do not correspond to any predefined default battery the text
will be 'user defined'.
When a default battery is selected the Use
tubular plate traction battery curve setting is always cleared. Changing
this setting afterwards has no effect on the default battery field.
Below is a table for a 12V battery. When using 24V or 48V just multiply
the voltages by 2 or 4.
User default types can be created. Just set the correct values for the
above mentioned settings and press the 'create new type' button in the
'select battery type' dialog box.
Note: User defined types are
stored locally on the PC and cannot be exported to other PC's.

help.title: Weak AC Input
help.text:
Weak AC input should be checked in cases where problems during charge
arise. Some generators generate a waveform which makes it difficult to
charge with the normal charge mechanism. If this option is checked another
mechanism is used which will enable the device to charge under practically
all conditions.
Disadvantage of using this option is that the power factor will be less
than 1.
Note: This option has no effect on the charge characteristic.

help.title: Stop after 10 Hr bulk
help.text:
This is a safety setting. When the bulk phase lasts more than 10 hours
this can be an indication that a battery cell is damaged. The absorption
voltage (or the 14.4V when BatterySafe
mode is used) will never be reached in that case and the other cells will
be over-charged resulting in the production of an explosive gas.
Therefore the charger is disabled if the bulk phase lasts more than
10 hours.
This setting can be disabled because it does not always indicate a problem
when the bulk phase lasts very long. The charge current can be very low
due to limited AC input current and/or AC loads. Also DC loads can "steal
away" part of the charge current. In that case the bulk phase will
need more time to complete and this setting must be disabled.
Note that there is no safety check against
over-charging when this settings is disabled!

help.title: Storage mode

If this option is checked the charge curve will be adapted in such a
way that when during absorption the current gets as low as 10% of the

This is used for tubular plate traction batteries. In the figure below

help.title: Charge curve
help.text:
With this setting one can choose between three different charge curves:
Fixed
Adaptive
Adaptive + BatterySafe
The Fixed charge curve will
have a fixed absorption time
The Adaptive and Adaptive
+ BatterySafe curves derive the absorption time from the Bulk time.
The maximum absorption time of these charge curves is determined by the
absorption time setting.
The Adaptive + BatterySafe curve
has a special regulation in the absorption phase. The absorption phase
will start when the voltage reaches 14.4V (for a 12V battery) regardless
of the specified absorption voltage. During the absorption phase the voltage
will increase with a fixed ramp until the voltage reaches the absorption
voltage or until the calculated absorption time is over. In the latter
case the absorption phase will end before the absorption voltage is reached.
Please refer to the manual for a more detailed description of the charge
process.

help.title: Introduction to VirtualSwitch
help.text:
( Virtual switch examples )
The VirtualSwitch page is the place where all VirtualSwitch settings
must be done.
The VirtualSwitch (VS) is an imaginary on/off switch in the software.
The VS is "switched" by the software when certain conditions
are met. The conditions which will cause the VS to switch on and off can
be configured by the user. This can be done on the extra tab pages:
Virtual switch on
conditions (A)
Virtual switch
off conditions (B)
Virtual switch options
Besides the 'regular' Virtual switch, a secondary Virtual switch is
available in some devices . The settings for the secondary Virtual
switch are on a separate tab page:
Ignore AC input
/ Generator control
One or more of these pages will become visible when a usage is specified
on the Virtual switch usage
page .
Regular Virtual switch
The conditions on the A-page have priority over the conditions on the
B-page. So switching the VS on has priority over switching it off. This
means that as long as a switch on condition is true the switch will be
on, regardless of the switch off conditions! A condition can be disabled
by setting its corresponding time to -1.
When the switch switches from off to on all the off-conditions are reset
so delays are measured from this point. An example makes this more
clear:
We specify that the VS goes on after UBat<10.9V
for 5 seconds ( how? )
and that the VS goes off 50 seconds after the load is lower than 200Watt
( how? ).
In the situation that the load is lower than
200 Watt and UBat drops below 10.9V the VS goes on and stays on as long
as UBat is lower than 10.9V. If UBat becomes higher than 10.9V within
50 seconds then the VS will stay on for 50 seconds (measured from the
switch on moment). Even if the load was lower than 200 Watt for hours!
One should keep in mind that the VS is imaginary. To give the VS a function
one must configure the VS to drive something ( how? ).
The VS can drive the multifunctional relay or it can be used to ignore
the AC input. What the VS drives is selected on the Virtual
switch usage page with the radio buttons. One must first give the
VS a function before the on- and off-conditions can be specified.
Ignoring the AC input with the VS can be useful when one wants to give
priority to the inverter.
Normally, inverting has lower priority than switching through the incoming
AC. Ignoring AC is specially designed for solar or wind generator systems.
Energy will only be taken from mains when there is not enough sunlight
or wind.
A note on timing accuracy: The delay times specified can in real life
be up to 1 unit shorter. So specifying 30 seconds will result in a delay
between 29 and 30 seconds. Specifying a delay of 45 minutes will result
in a delay between 44 and 45 minutes.

usage

With this setting one can specify how the VirtualSwitch is used. One
can choose to connect the VirtualSwitch to the multifunctional (auxiliary)
relay which gives the possibility to drive almost anything with the VirtualSwitch.
The other option is to use the VirtualSwitch to ignore the AC input. This
can be useful in solar or wind generator applications. Energy will only
be taken from the mains when there is not enough sunlight or wind.
Some devices
support secondary virtual switch settings (see secondary
virtual switch: Ignore AC input / Generator control ).
In such devices it is possible to use the primary
'regular' virtual switch settings or the secondary virtual switch settings
or both.
When both are used, one of them drives the auxiliary relay and the other
is used for Ignoring the AC input.

help.title: secondary virtual switch tab
help.text:
secondary virtual switch: Ignore AC
input / Generator control
This secondary virtual switch page allows you to specify additional
settings, independent of the 'regular' virtual switch settings which are
on the pages: Virtual switch
on conditions (A) , Virtual
switch off conditions (B) and Virtual
switch options
The content of this page varies slightly depending on the usage
specified.
When the 'regular' virtual switch is used to drive the multifunctional
relay, this page can be used to ignore the incoming AC and vice versa.
Because the multifunctional relay, when driven by the conditions on
this page, will normally be used to start/stop a generator, this page
is called 'Generator control' in that case. However, the relay can be
used for any purpose.
The main difference between the 'regular' virtual switch conditions
and the conditions on this page is that the conditions on this page are
independent of each other. The device remembers the history of each condition.
The example below illustrates this difference.
example:
Assume we want to ignore the AC input as long as the load is lower than
1000W and the battery voltage is higher than 13.5V.
To prevent unstable situations we have to set different limits for not ignoring.
We choose to not-ignore when the load is higher than 1500W or the
battery voltage is lower than 12V.
Assume the situation is stable and
we have a load of 500W and a battery voltage of 14V. The result is
that we ignore the incoming AC.
Now the load increases to 2000W and
we assume the battery voltage stays the same. The AC input will not
be ignored anymore and if there is a valid AC input signal the device
will switch to mains and start charging. (Assuming the charger is
enabled)
Then the load drops to 1300W. At this
point the difference between the 'regular' virtual switch settings
and the settings on this page becomes clear.
If we used the 'regular' virtual switch settings to perform this
action the result would be that the AC input will be ignored when
the load drops to 1300W.
Explanation :
The usage would be specified as 'VS used to ignore AC input'
The on-conditions would
be:
load higher than 1500W
Udc lower than 12V
The off-conditions would
be:
load lower than 1000W
Udc higher than 13.5V
Since there is no on-condition
valid (load is 1300W and Udc is 14V) the off-conditions are tested. Since
at least one off-condition is valid (Udc is higher than 13.5V) the Virtual
switch will switch off so the AC input will be ignored.
If we used the settings on this page to ignore the AC input, the
AC input would still be not-ignored when the load drops to 1300W.
The reason for this is
that the device 'remembers' that the AC input is allowed
due to a high load and it will not start ignoring the AC input before
the load drops to a value lower than 1000W. Independent of the Udc level.

help.title: secondary VS condition invert auxiliary relay driving
help.text:
secondary VS condition: invert auxiliary relay
driving
This setting is on the secondary virtual switch Ignore
AC input / Generator control tab.
If this check box is unchecked the auxiliary relay (sometimes also called
multifunctional relay) will be driven when the generator has to start.
When the generator has to stop the auxiliary relay will be released.
If this check box is checked the driving is inverse. This can, for instance,
be used in fail safe systems. If someone switches the device off, the relay is certainly not driven
and so the generator will start (when correctly wired).
